newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-RADFORD QUITS TOP BRITISH POST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-RADFORD QUITS TOP BRITISH POST.

text.p: Peter Radford quit on Saturday as executive chairman of the troubled British Athletics Federation (BAF) just two weeks after the sacking of the federation's public relations officer Tony Ward.
In a surprise announcement, the 57-year-old former Olympic sprinter said he was stepping down to take a job as professor and head of sports sciences at a university near London.
Radford, appointed in February 1994, recently received the backing of both his management board and the British Athletes' Association (BAA) and Saturday's news was not expected.
He said he was sorry to be leaving but felt British athletics was "in a good position for the future."

BAA director Geoff Parsons said he had heard the announcement "with the deepest regret" and described Radford as "an individual of both vision and intellect who has at all times conducted his affairs with the greatest integrity."
But Ward launched a fierce attack on Radford, who he said was instrumental in his dismissal.
"I don't think he's achieved anything over the last three years and the sport is in a desperate situation," he said.
"During my last two or three months in the job I was dismayed at the way the sport was going. He seemed to me to be leading British athletics down a blind alley."
A replacement for Radford has not yet been named.
